name: level1-playthrough-win
description:
Level 1 (Dusty Hollow) playthrough under #553's physical drilling: a survey, one blast cycle (of an originally-planned two), and vehicle-hauled contract fulfillment. Originally named for an $80k profit target and scoped for 3 blast cycles; Findings #45-51 already showed that target unreachable even pre-#553 -- the file's original sequence never bought a vehicle, named building types that don't exist, and used a silently-rejected assign_skill syntax, so no material ever reached storage. #553 turns `drill_plan` into a real queue -- a licensed driller must physically drive a `drill_rig` to each hole, one at a time -- and lands a brand-new `staffed:true` primitive alongside it: a free driller+drill_rig, blaster, and 3 drivers (5 employees, 4 vehicles), at zero cost, before any assertion. Two new, load-bearing findings surface here specifically, because `campaign start level:dusty_hollow staffed:true` is a combination no earlier #553 fix (tutorial-playthrough.json, blast-basic.json) exercised: dusty_hollow's own terrain, not tutorial_pit's or sandbox new_game's.

Finding (vehicle deadlock, unchanged): staffed:true spawns its 4 free vehicles nose-to-tail along z=2 at x=0,2,4,6 -- the drill_rig (vehicle #1) is the outermost. dusty_hollow's terrain makes the A*-cheapest route from (0,2) toward the blast site run straight through the other three parked vehicles' cells, and `tickVehicleOnNavGrid` (EntityMovementTick.ts) recomputes that exact route every tick -- occupancy is not part of path cost -- then blocks on the immediate-next-step occupancy check (`isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle`) forever, since none of the other three vehicles ever move on their own. Confirmed directly: the drill_rig sits welded to (1,2) for 300+ ticks with zero progress, for any target requiring eastward travel, until the blocking vehicles are moved out of the way -- moving just the immediate blocker forward reveals the same wall one vehicle further down the line. A real player hits an identical dead end; nothing in the game auto-clears a parked vehicle out of another one's path. Worked around here (not fixed -- an engine gap, out of scope for a scenario-def fix) by relocating the three non-drilling free vehicles off the corridor with `vehicle move` before assigning the driller to the rig -- a real, player-clickable action (select the vehicle's Fleet panel row, click MOVE HERE; vehicle-traffic.json already exercises this exact click path for the same command).

Finding (bankruptcy, #557, fixed): #553's real per-hole drilling and #554's real per-hole charging time made this file's own ORIGINAL crew (13 employees -- staffed:true's free 5 plus 8 hand-hired, several boosted to skill level 5) unaffordable on dusty_hollow's $50,000 starting budget and `BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100` (Bankruptcy.ts, threshold $5,000): payroll for 13 people, even sandbox-tested down to Rookie/level-1 qualifications across six separate crew configurations, drained faster than dusty_hollow's economy could ever recover within the ~100+ ticks drilling and charging a truncated 4-hole pattern actually take, seizing the mine by bankruptcy at cumulative tick 119 every time. The actual root cause was never skill level or drilling time on their own -- it was headcount: `employee list` right after the blast on the pre-fix file showed only 3 of the 13 employees (driller #1, blaster #2, and the surveyor) ever did anything at all; the other 10 (a backup surveyor, 2 extra drillers, 2 extra blasters, 2 extra drivers, all boosted to level 5) sat idle at spawn the entire file, drawing full salary for zero benefit -- staffed:true's own free crew already covers drilling (driller #1), charging (blaster #2), and hauling (driver #3, already licensed driving.truck) without hiring anyone extra. Fixed by hiring only what this file's own actions actually use: one surveyor. That alone drops the crew to 6 and keeps cash's one post-charge dip below the $5,000 threshold well short of the 100-tick grace window, sandbox-confirmed end-to-end -- `bankrupt` stays false all the way to the file's own scripted end. `BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD`/`GRACE_TICKS`/`BASE_SALARIES`/`QUALIFICATION_SALARY_BONUS` (shared game balance, out of scope for a single scenario file) are untouched.

What the file proves end-to-end: blast with only the 4 holes a lone driller can land inside dusty_hollow's runway. Voxel/fragment yield scales off charge density, not the full 16-hole plan, so a genuinely truncated pattern still rates PERFECT and produces hundreds of fragments -- drilling, charging, sequencing, blasting, three real deaths (the two blasting-qualified employees this crew actually has, plus the surveyor caught near the blast), self-dispatched hauling (#552), and one full contract cycle all still happen for real. The drill_rig itself survives the blast and keeps working the remaining ordered holes afterward, though not fast enough to land a full second pattern before the file's own scripted end. A second pattern, a second contract cycle, and the original $80k target are still out of reach within this file's own step count -- not from an authoring mistake, but because #553/#554 make a full 16-hole pattern genuinely slow -- but the mine survives to the file's own end this time, cash deep in the red but never seized.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, before any assertion: employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1), #2 blaster (blasting lvl1), #3/#4/#5 drivers (driving.truck/driving.excavator/driving.excavator lvl1), vehicle #1 drill_rig, #2 debris_hauler, #3 rock_digger, #4 rock_fragmenter (all tier 1, all unmanned). Free -- cash is unaffected, still $50,000, matching dusty_hollow's own default. Left as `equals` (issue #596): this is the file's first step, so there is no prior-step "before" cash for `changedBy` to diff against -- the evaluator reads it as 0, not the pre-game state.

New finding (see file description): the free debris_hauler (#2) is the first of three parked vehicles standing directly in drill_rig #1's only cheap route east -- confirmed directly by sandbox trace, the rig sits welded to (1,2) for 300+ ticks otherwise, for any target requiring eastward travel. Relocated off the corridor before the driller ever tries to drive anywhere. `vehicle move` is a real, player-clickable action -- select the vehicle's Fleet panel row, click MOVE HERE -- the same click path vehicle-traffic.json already exercises for this exact command. Row-select click scoped to the card's name column (`> div:first-child > div:nth-child(2)`, the head row's nameCol -- vehicle type name + id text), not the bare `[data-vehicle-id]` row: confirmed directly in real interaction-mode CI and reproduced locally (orderedHoleCount stuck at 16 -- see Finding below) that Puppeteer's default click lands on the row's bounding-box CENTER, and FleetPanel.ts's row-click handler bails out (`target.closest('button, select, input, a')`) whenever that center falls on the driver-assign control instead of open card space. debris_hauler's extra load-gauge row (makeLoadGauge, FleetPanel.ts -- the only role that gets one) happens to push its card's center off the assign row, so this vehicle's own row-click looked fine in isolation; #3/#4 below (no load gauge, shorter cards) are the ones this actually broke. `.bs-fleet-hp`/`.bs-fleet-status` were tried first and rejected -- FleetPanel.ts's `refreshDynamic` replaceWith()s both classes' elements on every panel poll (their signature -- vehicle id/type/tier/driverId -- doesn't change from a move alone, so every poll takes the cheap incremental path), racing Puppeteer's own scroll-then-click against a live DOM swap. `nameCol` is untouched by that path (only `render()`'s full rebuild ever replaces it), so it doesn't race.

The second blocker in line -- clearing #2 alone only reveals rock_digger (#3) welded to the next cell over, confirmed directly. Panel already open from the step above; re-clicking the toolbar tab here would toggle it closed (UIManager.togglePanel, the same trap #552's contract-deliver note already documents), so this step does not. Root-cause finding (real interaction-mode CI failure, 'orderedHoleCount should be 12 but is 16'): rock_digger's card has no load gauge (debris_hauler-only, makeLoadGauge), so it's shorter than #2's card, and a click on the bare `[data-vehicle-id="3"]` row lands dead-center on the driver-assign control -- FleetPanel.ts's row handler treats that as a control click, not a select, and never fires onSelectVehicleCb. Confirmed directly: `#bs-selection-bar .bsx-mono` still read "#2 · Idle" after this click, so the whole rest of the step (cameraFocus/move_here) silently re-issued vehicle #2's own move again -- vehicle #3 never received a move order, the corridor stayed blocked, and the driller deadlocked with 0 holes landed. A prior fix pass (commit c44d23e) diagnosed this as a stale drag-rectangle/spacing-stepper mismatch on the drill_plan step and left this step's selector untouched -- that diagnosis was wrong for this file (the drill_plan grid math here was already correct: dragTiles 15,15->25,25 at the grid tool's own 3m default spacing yields exactly the declared 4x4). Fixed by scoping the click to the card's nameCol (`> div:first-child > div:nth-child(2)`), a plain non-interactive block present on every card regardless of height and never replaced by FleetPanel.ts's incremental refresh path (unlike `.bs-fleet-hp`/`.bs-fleet-status`, which are, and raced Puppeteer's click when tried first), so the click always lands on open card space and reaches the row's own select handler. Second, independent bug hiding behind the first: once selection genuinely reached vehicle #3, screen-center `mousemove x:640` still failed to move it -- a screenshot taken mid-step (`__renderFrame`-forced, matching the camera's real state) shows the cursor's own hover tooltip reading "Rock Digger / Idle · HP 150" AT screen center, i.e. `cameraFocus(4.5,6.5,25)` points the ray straight through rock_digger's own body (still parked at (4,2), same X as its target) before it ever reaches the ground at (4.5,6.5) -- `scenePicking.aim.terrain` resolves to nothing (a vehicle was hit, not terrain), so `move_here`'s `if (!terrain)` guard fires a silent `no_move_target` toast and no console command is ever dispatched. Confirmed directly: `vehicle list` right after this click still showed rock_digger `task: idle` at its start position -- 0 ticks had even elapsed, so any successful move would already read `task: moving`, exactly like #2's own vehicle-list check one step earlier. Moving the mouse pixel off-center (`x:750`) instead of the camera target clears the occlusion (`vehicle list` shows `task: moving`); a raycast that far off-center, this close to the camera, lands on a wildly different world point at this perspective/pitch (confirmed directly: resolves to (10,-2), nowhere near (4,6)) -- fine for this step's own purpose (get rock_digger off the corridor, cash unaffected, nothing else asserts its landing tile) and, confirmed directly by running the full scenario to its end, this landing spot does not sit in any other vehicle's later path. An intermediate attempt tried shifting the *camera focus target* by one metre in X instead (keeping the cursor dead-center) to land closer to the declared tile -- it broke the occlusion too and landed nearer (5,9) -- but that spot turned out to sit squarely in debris_hauler #2's own hauling route: `contract deliver` below stalled forever (`storedMassKg` stuck at 0, debris_hauler frozen mid-tile at (4.12,8.12) for 10+ ticks, task still reading `moving`), the same occupancy-blocks-pathing class of bug the file's own vehicle-deadlock finding already documents, just triggered by a well-meaning `vehicle move` destination instead of staffed:true's own spawn layout. Reverted to the cursor-offset landing since a `vehicle move` step's own destination precision is not itself under test here, only that the corridor clears and nothing downstream gets blocked -- confirmed by a full scenario run reaching `contract deliver` successfully with this landing tile.

The third and last blocker (rock_fragmenter). With all three off the z=2 corridor, drill_rig #1's route east is genuinely clear -- confirmed directly (sandbox trace: 40 ticks door-to-door to (15,15) once unblocked, vs. never before). Kept close (z=6, not far off-site) rather than parked deep off-map, so debris_hauler #2 still has a short trip back once hauling self-dispatches after the blast -- Finding (bankruptcy) below is tight enough that a long hauler commute would cost this file its one contract delivery too. Same two bugs as #3's step above, fixed the same way: the row click is scoped to nameCol (rock_fragmenter has no load gauge either), and `mousemove` targets `x:750` rather than dead-center -- `cameraFocus(6.5,6.5,25)` puts rock_fragmenter's own body (parked at (6,2), same X as its target) directly in the screen-center raycast, same occlusion as rock_digger's. Landing tile ((11,1), confirmed directly) is off in a different direction from rock_digger's and, confirmed the same way (a full scenario run reaching `contract deliver`), does not sit in debris_hauler's hauling route either.

#553: staffed:true's free driller (employee #1, already licensed blasting lvl1 + driving.drill_rig lvl1) boards the free drill_rig (vehicle #1). Without a driver the rig is a mesh and no drill_hole action ever starts.

#557/new finding (payroll-vs-bankruptcy): this file's original crew (13 employees, 8 hand-hired on top of staffed:true's 5 free ones) burned payroll faster than dusty_hollow's $50,000 budget and #553/#554's real drilling+charging time could ever recover from -- sandbox-confirmed bankruptcy at cumulative tick 119 regardless of skill-level tuning, since even at Rookie/level-1 qualifications a 13-person crew's BASE salaries alone outrun the budget over the 100+ ticks this file's drilling+charging phase actually takes. Of the file's original 8 hires, only a single surveyor is genuinely load-bearing: staffed:true's own free crew already covers drilling (driller #1, licensed driving.drill_rig + blasting), charging (blaster #2, licensed blasting), and hauling (drivers #3/#4/#5, licensed driving.truck/excavator) -- the file's original extra hires (a backup surveyor, 2 more drillers, 2 more blasters, 2 more drivers, all boosted to level 5) never did anything: sandbox-confirmed via `employee list` right after the blast on the pre-fix file, only #1 (free driller), #2 (free blaster) and the surveyor ever worked or died -- the other 7 hires sat idle at spawn (82,34) the entire file, drawing full boosted salary for nothing. Hiring only what this file's own actions actually use closes the gap without touching BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD/GRACE_TICKS/BASE_SALARIES/QUALIFICATION_SALARY_BONUS (out of scope, shared game balance) -- sandbox-confirmed end-to-end with this fix: cash dips negative post-charge but `bankrupt` stays false all the way through the file's own scripted end.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification; this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`. Employee ids renumbered +5 throughout for staffed:true's 5 free hires (was #1 pre-staffed).

Finding #47 (unchanged): the only warehouse type is `freight_warehouse` (Building.ts/balance.ts). Placed at (5,5), outside the blast footprint -- see Finding #47's original note for the full reasoning (a first attempt closer to the blast site got destroyed by a blast's clear radius).

#552/#557: staffed:true's free debris_hauler (vehicle #2) is reused here rather than buying a second one by hand -- the file's own hauling volume (one 260kg rubble delivery this cycle, matching Finding #48's fragment-matching constraint below) never needs a second hauler, and this file's budget cannot spare a manual purchase on top of everything else. #557: this file no longer hires its own driver (see the hire step's own finding) -- staffed:true's own free driver #3 (already licensed driving.truck lvl1 from the free roster) boards it instead. Re-opens the vehicles panel first (UIManager.togglePanel, same pattern as level2-playthrough-win's fix): the panel had switched to employees then build (the surveyor hire and the freight_warehouse placement above), so #bs-vehicle-panel's own [data-vehicle-id="2"] row was off-screen (display:none, zero size) at this point -- not a stale selector, the panel itself just wasn't the active one. togglePanel only closes an ALREADY-active panel, so this click safely switches to vehicles rather than toggling it shut. `.bs-vehicle-assign-btn` (`makeAssignRow`, fleetDetailSections.ts) reads a `<select>` next to it, not a fixed target -- clicking Assign without first choosing an option in that select just assigns whoever the browser's default selection lands on (its first eligible option). Fixed with a `set` action on the row's own `select` (scoped by `[data-vehicle-id="2"]`, matching the file's other dropdown-driven steps) before the Assign click, mirroring the Charge step's own real-control convention (issue #515) rather than relying on whatever the dropdown defaulted to -- here that default happens to already be employee #3, but the explicit `set` keeps this step's own intent ("employee #3 boards") true regardless of roster order.

Finding #49 (unchanged): seismic ($3000) is unaffordable this late in setup; core_sample alone ($800) sends employee #6 (first hired surveyor) to survey (15,15), which the blast below then clears. #553/new: unlike the pre-#553 file, this survey now has time to actually finish -- ground rule #14's arrival-gating raced the surveyor against the blast, and pre-#553 the blast (an instant command) always won; now the driller needs 60 real ticks to land even a truncated pattern, so the survey completes long before the blast fires this time -- surveyCount below stays 0 only because 0 ticks have elapsed since this step, not because the result never arrives (see the closing surveyCount:1).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Ground rule #15: depth corrected to 6, matching the grid-tool's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M. #553: confirming the grid only orders the 16 holes -- they are ghosts until the driller drives drill_rig #1 to each one, so holeCount is 0 here.

#553: sandbox-measured. The lone driller lands only 4 of the pattern's 16 holes in this window -- not the full drain the pattern set out to order. Landing all 16 (tutorial-playthrough.json's own solo-driller measurement: ~400 ticks for the same size pattern) would keep this file's cash below the $5,000 bankruptcy threshold for well over the 100-tick grace period (Bankruptcy.ts) -- see the file description's bankruptcy finding. This file blasts with the 4 that land instead of waiting for the rest, the only way any of drilling/blasting/hauling/contract-fulfillment survives to be exercised at all. Holes 5-16 never land: the pad stops here on purpose, not because 60 was too small a guess.

#554/new finding: charging is now real, queued work (one `charge_hole` action per hole, landed by a blaster physically walking to the hole) -- draining the charge queue below takes dozens of real ticks, during which drill_rig #1 (still holding 12 more ordered holes) keeps drilling regardless, landing 4 more holes inside that same window (confirmed directly: sandbox trace, holeCount 4->8 across the charge-wait alone). `sequence auto` sequences every currently-drilled hole unconditionally (autoVPattern over ctx.state.drillHoles, DrillPlan.ts) and `blast`'s own validateBlastPlan (BlastPlan.ts) requires a charge AND a sequence delay for every drilled hole with no partial-pattern option -- so any hole that lands after the charge order was placed can never be blasted without re-charging it, and re-charging costs further real ticks that let the driller land still more holes, a divergence that only resolves once the full 16-hole pattern is drilled (confirmed directly, sandbox trace across 3 recharge rounds: holeCount 4->8->12->15 and climbing), busting this file's own already-documented bankruptcy runway long before a second blast could ever happen. #553's own drilling-time budget and #554's own charging-time budget were each individually calibrated against an INSTANT partner action; wired together, the driller has nothing to stop it from outrunning the deliberately-truncated 4-hole pattern the instant charging needs its own real time too. Fixed the same way a player would: cancelling the 12 still-ordered (never-drilled) holes right after the tick-60 cutoff and before charging starts, via the Drill panel's own per-hole delete button (`drill_plan remove hole:<id>`, Drill.ts's `makeOrderedHoleRow` -- a real, player-clickable control, not a console-only shortcut). With nothing left ordered, the driller has no more work once its current in-flight hole (if any) finishes, so no ticks spent waiting on the charge queue ever grow holeCount past 4 again -- holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount converge cleanly at 4 instead of chasing a moving target. Ordered rows render before drilled rows in the panel (DrillStep.render, `...ordered.map(...), ...holes.map(...)`), so the SAME selector, clicked repeatedly, always removes the first remaining ORDERED hole -- never one of the 4 already-drilled ones -- letting this single selector serve for all 12 clicks. New finding: the driller (and any other blasting-qualified employee freed up once its own task ends) gets auto-dispatched to charge a hole in person and doesn't proactively leave once done -- so unlike the pre-#554 file (deathCount 1, only the surveyor near the survey tile), several of the employees who physically loaded a charge are still standing on their hole when it fires. See the blast step below for the resulting death toll, sandbox-confirmed and now hard-asserted for real. Panel auto-navigates to step 2 (Charge) the instant any drilled hole is uncharged (suggestStep, BlastWorkshop.ts) -- true here well before all 16 land -- so the Drill step (and its remove-hole buttons) would otherwise render display:none. A real player clicks back onto tab 1 first; that one manual click also disables autoAdvance (setActiveStep(step, true)), so it stays pinned through all 12 removals below.
Last of the 12 cancellations -- drill plan now holds exactly the 4 already-landed holes and nothing more, matching this file's original, deliberately-truncated pattern.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed. `charge-all` only ever reaches the 4 already-drilled holes -- the 12 still-ordered ones are not chargeable yet, matching chargedCount below.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.
This value already matches the Sequence panel's own 25ms default (Sequence.ts DEFAULT_DELAY_STEP_MS) -- 0 stepper clicks needed, asserted rather than assumed (Finding #75).

Finding #46 (renumbered, same reasoning): employee #6 (the surveyor dispatched to survey (15,15)) is standing at/near that tile when this 4-hole blast clears it -- a real, reproducible casualty. Rated PERFECT with hundreds of fragments despite only 4 of 16 holes firing -- yield scales off charge density, not pattern completeness, sandbox-confirmed directly (302 fragments, 236 cleared voxels). Real root cause of the command-vs-interaction split previously documented here (deathCount 2 vs 1, vehicleCount 3 vs 4): the drill_plan step above was missing `diameter:` -- the same class of bug vibration-budget.json's own history already found and fixed (see that file's finances-step note) -- so command mode's `drill_hole` actions ran at mining.ts's console-only fallback diameter (0.15m) while interaction mode's real grid-tool click always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M (0.089m, Drill.ts); computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales duration by diameter, so the smaller real diameter drills measurably faster. With no diameter: specified, command mode's driller had less spare time left in this file's 60-tick drilling window and stayed idle at (22,15), parked among the holes it just drilled and inside this blast's radius. Fixed by adding diameter:0.089 to the drill_plan command, matching the real click exactly. `deathCount` updated for #557 (this file's crew shrunk to just staffed:true's 5 free employees plus one hired surveyor -- see the earlier hire step's own finding): drill_rig #1 itself still survives (its driver, employee #1, was mid rest-cycle and dismounted onto the vehicle's own position by #593's fix, then the 12 hole-cancellation steps above froze it there for good -- outside this blast's radius, matching `vehicleCount`:4 below) -- but charging is real, in-person work (#554): every blasting-qualified employee the game auto-dispatched to load one of the 4 charges walked to that hole and stayed there once done. With only two blasting-qualified employees left in this crew (driller #1 once its drilling task ends, and free blaster #2), both of them plus the surveyor #6 (from the original finding above) are the toll -- sandbox-confirmed directly (`employee list` right after the blast: #1, #2, #6 DEAD, #3/#4/#5 unaffected) -- three casualties, not five, now that this file no longer hires extra blasters/drillers who never did any of the charging.

wellBeing dropped from this equals block (issue #596's own rule): it settles wherever the charge-wait above (#554, real ticks now) happened to leave it, not a value this step's own read-only `scores` call moves or that the scenario's narrative depends on -- exactly the incidental-checkpoint case the rule calls out, so it is not re-captured as another precise float. safety/ecology/nuisance are still the file's own point here (unaffected by the blast at this exact instant, before any post-blast events fire) and stay hard-asserted.

#553/new: a `lucky_strike` event is already pending the instant this tick is requested (fired as a side effect of the blast above) -- 0 of the 10 requested ticks advance; the tick command itself refuses until the event is resolved, same as every other pending-event guard in this file. tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): its own point is that the pending event blocks the whole batch, not a specific running total -- robust to the charge-wait above (#554) landing on a different real-tick total.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. `lucky_strike`'s option 0 is a fixed $10,000 windfall ("A cash bonus goes straight to the company account for the unexpectedly rich yield") -- deterministic under this file's fixed seed, not the reason this file survives (still nowhere close to offsetting setup cost -- see the file description's bankruptcy finding).

Run the warehouse ordered above out to a standing building (#556). Placed here rather than at the order: everything above is pinned to an exact tickCount, to the blast’s own outcome, or to the event that interrupts the tick block just before it, and the warehouse is not read until the hauling that feeds the rubble_disposal delivery below.

Finding #48 (unchanged): the Fleet panel's Haul button always sends the vehicle to `findReachableGroundFragment` -- the NEAREST reachable, non-oversized fragment, with no regard for ore content -- and #552 self-dispatches hauling automatically, so a player cannot target a specific fragment by ore at all. The contract must match what the hauler will actually claim, not the reverse: this cycle's nearest reachable fragment carries no named ore, so the rubble-disposal contract (materialId '') is the one it can satisfy, confirmed by replaying this file's own exact command sequence. #554: this contract's id has renumbered across runs (the charge-wait's real, queued `charge_hole` work consumes a different slice of the contract-generation RNG stream than instant-charge timing did) -- #635 drops the numeric id entirely in favor of the stable `type:rubble_disposal` selector (materialId '' for this type, so no `material:` clause), which resolves to whichever rubble-disposal contract the generator produced this run without needing to track its id. New finding, real interaction-mode CI: this step used to sit right after `contract list`, before the tick-10/event-choose pair above -- but `lucky_strike` (fired as a side effect of the blast, several steps up) is already pending by then, and unlike command mode, where a pending event is just state until something reads it, a real browser shows its modal (`.bs-confirm-overlay`) the instant it goes pending, sitting over the whole shell and blocking this step's own toolbar click (confirmed directly: `clickSelector` failed with "covered by div.bs-confirm-overlay"). Moved to after the tick-10/event-choose pair instead, which the file was already going to run anyway -- `lucky_strike` is resolved for real by the time this step's click reaches the toolbar, in both modes.
tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning -- robust to the charge-wait above (#554) landing on a different real-tick total.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered.
tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning -- robust to the charge-wait above (#554) landing on a different real-tick total.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons.

#552: hauling self-dispatched automatically once debris_hauler #2 (relocated close to the blast site, not off-map -- see the vehicle-move steps above) had somewhere to go; 30 ticks (the 3 tick-10 steps above) was enough for a full round trip and back, confirmed directly (storedMassKg > 260 by this point). One haul is enough to complete this 260kg contract outright, same as the pre-#552 flow's own single-haul sizing. #635: dropped the numeric contract id (it renumbered across runs -- see the accept step's own finding) for the stable `type:rubble_disposal` selector, which resolves to this run's rubble-disposal contract regardless of its id. tickCount converted to `changedBy: 0` (issue #596) -- this step is itself a non-ticking console call, its own point is that delivery doesn't advance the clock, not a specific running total. deathCount 3, matching the blast step's own #557 finding (charging-in-person casualties, now a 2-person blasting crew plus the surveyor rather than the pre-#557 5).
tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning -- robust to upstream timing shifting the real-tick total this step starts from.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons.

Sandbox-confirmed: only 1 of the 10 requested ticks advances here -- a spontaneous event goes pending mid-batch (same `tick` guard as every other pending-event interruption in this file) after just 1 tick rather than after the full 10, unlike the other `tick 10` steps in this stretch. Left as `increased` rather than a pinned `changedBy` count -- the exact tick this particular event happens to interrupt on is incidental to what this step is testing (that the clock keeps moving at all), not the step's own subject.
